gp.text: The $233 increase in Adjusted EBITDA for the three months ended March 31, 2026, was primarily driven by higher project throughput, particularly on lump-sum, fixed-price contracts, as well as a modest improvement in gross profit margin compared to the same period in 2025. This stronger operating performance contributed to a $270 improvement in net income, from a net loss of $29 in the prior-year quarter to net income of $241 in the current quarter.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales
cor.text:
Cost of sales increased 55% from the first quarter of 2025 to the first quarter of 2026, generally consistent with higher revenue activity. The rate of increase was slightly below revenue growth, resulting in an improvement in gross profit margins to 32% of sales, up from 31% in the prior year period. Operating leverage from higher throughput was partially offset by increased Brazil office expenses and higher consumables costs associated with fabrication projects.

The Company records depreciation expense related to revenue-generating property, plant and equipment as cost of sales, which totaled $146 and $117 for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

ga.heading: Selling, general and administrative expenses
ga.text:
Selling, general and administrative expenses increased by $611 in the first quarter of 2026 compared to the first quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher administrative headcount, resulting in a $405 increase in personnel costs, as well as a $156 increase in audit fees and $50 of public company expenses and other costs.

The Company records depreciation expense related to administrative property, plant and equipment and intellectual property as SG&A, which totaled $32 and $29 for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

The rate of increase was above revenue growth, resulting in a 5% decrease in gross profit margin to 27% of sales, compared to 32% in the prior-year period. A greater share of contracts in the current period included significant cost-plus components, which was the primary reason for the decrease. Under these arrangements, we earn a markup on costs incurred, which generally produces a lower gross margin percentage.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales
cor.text:
Cost of sales increased 75% from the third quarter of 2025 to the third quarter of 2026, generally consistent with higher revenue activity. The rate of increase was above revenue growth, resulting in a 5% decrease in gross profit margin to 27% of sales, compared to 32% in the prior-year period. A greater share of contracts in the current period included significant cost-plus components, which was the primary reason for the decrease. Under these arrangements, we earn a markup on costs incurred, which generally produces a lower gross margin percentage.

The Company records depreciation expense related to revenue-generating property, plant and equipment as cost of sales, which totaled $197 and $124 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

ga.heading: Selling, general and administrative expenses
ga.text:
Selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A”) decreased approximately $187 during the third quarter of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to a $562 reduction in Other G&A expenses, largely due to the $569 of bad debt expense related to OMSi recorded in the prior-year period, with no comparable expense in the current year. Additional decreases included $85 in legal and corporate expenses and $21 in professional fees. These decreases were partially offset by increases related to corporate growth of $198 in personnel-related expenses, $88 in information technology, $70 in insurance, and $125 across various other accounts.

The Company records depreciation expense related to administrative property, plant and equipment and intellectual property as SG&A, which totaled $18 and $22 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Additional decreases included $85 in legal and corporate expenses and $21 in professional fees. These decreases were partially offset by increases related to corporate growth of $198 in personnel-related expenses, $88 in information technology, $70 in insurance, and $125 across various other accounts.

The Company records depreciation expense related to administrative property, plant and equipment and intellectual property as SG&A, which totaled $18 and $22 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Koil Energy is not dependent on a single customer, but our two largest customers together accounted for approximately 40% of revenue in 2025.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, our two largest customers accounted for 23 percent and 16 percent of total revenues, respectively.
For the year ended December 31, 2024, our two largest customers accounted for 47 percent and 27 percent of total revenues, respectively.
No other customers were in excess of 10 percent of revenues.
As of December 31, 2025, five of our customers accounted for 22 percent, 16 percent, 12 percent, 12 percent and 10 percent of total accounts receivable.
As of December 31, 2024, three of our customers accounted for 37 percent, 20 percent, and 14 percent of total accounts receivable.
Koil Energy’s facility in Houston, Texas, offers high quality warehousing and workshop capacity, external storage, and a strategic location near customers and key suppliers.
The amount and variety of our products and services required in a given period by a customer can depend upon the customer’s capital expenditure budget as well as the results of competitive bids.
The ultimate realization of the deferred tax assets depends upon our ability to generate sufficient taxable income of the appropriate character in the future.
The Company generally depends on cash on hand, cash flows from operations, and the potential opportunistic sales of property, plant and equipment (“PP&E”) to satisfy its liquidity needs.
